title: Reunion with the Black Organization
notes: Rebuilt from the full available transcripts of episodes 176 and 178. Episode 177 (the middle episode, presumably containing the party's early scenes, full Character Card introductions for the seven suspects, and more detail on Haibara's kidnapping) has NO subtitle file locally and is missing from this rebuild -- some suspect occupations (Nanjo, Mihei, Tarumi, Tawara, Mugikura) are therefore left null/unspecified because 176+178 never pair those names with an occupation (only Chris Vineyard='American actress' and Masuyama='big fish in finances' are explicitly tied to an occupation on screen). Neither available file contains a single (Flashback)-tagged line, so every edge below is temporal_frame:'present' (Haibara's opening nightmare about Gin killing the Detective Boys is tagged (Thoughts), i.e. an imagined dream, not a real backstory event, so it was NOT encoded as a kills/assault edge). Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shin'ichi Kudo, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Professor Agasa) omitted by convention as in ep011, even though Conan is the one who plants the transceiver bug and solves the case -- his role is implicit in the object/clue edges (e.g. the bug o7, the deduction clues cA-cC implicating Masuyama directly). The old wiki-summary case file (cases/ep176-178...) got the core whodunit right (Kenzo Masuyama a.k.a. Pisco killed lawyer Shigehiko Nomiguchi with a chandelier rigged via a silenced, handkerchief-muffled gunshot to its chain) but was drastically under-built: it had no event-free direct edges, invented a generic 'was_used_in'/'occurred_before' event-node schema now superseded, said only 'two witnesses cleared by alibi' when the transcript actually gives six suspects six DISTINCT, specific alibi reasons (Tawara & Chris directly under the chandelier with no angle to shoot; Mihei had the shot-through chain fragment flung into his own mouth; Mugikura was watched on stage; Tarumi & Nanjo were photographed embracing each other), and it completely omitted the larger Black-Organization frame story that makes up roughly half of both episodes: Conan and Haibara bugging Gin's Porsche, Gin/Vodka's phone call revealing the hit on Nomiguchi and codename 'Pisco', Haibara being captured and locked in a hotel wine cellar, her escape via a chimney, Gin shooting and nearly executing her on a rooftop, Vermouth (undercover in this case as suspect Chris Vineyard) secretly rescuing her AND secretly having supplied Masuyama's replacement handkerchief before police questioning (a fabricated-alibi prop, since his real one flew off with his bullet during the murder), and Gin's own execution of Masuyama on the Organization leadership's direct order after a photographer's candid shot exposed him -- followed by a cover-up (Masuyama's house burned down, Nomiguchi's family disappeared). Some details are genuinely ambiguous in the available transcript and are flagged in attrs rather than asserted as fact: whether Masuyama or someone else physically kidnapped Haibara, and the exact ignition source of the room 404 fire (likely tied to Conan's warning about the spilled Spirytus alcohol, but this is never shown on screen in 176/178). case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Of all the guests who received a purple handkerchief at Director Sakamaki's memorial party, most had already gone home by the time of the murder -- comparing the full guest list against who still possessed their handkerchief narrows the suspect pool down to just seven people, one of whom must be the shooter Pisco.

Masuyama's original purple handkerchief flew off with his bullet during the murder and was never recovered at the scene, yet he still had a matching handkerchief on him during the later police headcount -- the mismatch between the handkerchief that should be missing and the one he actually produced points to a secretly supplied replacement.

Cross-checking each of the seven remaining suspects' positions and alibis at the moment of the chandelier drop -- Tawara and Chris directly underneath with no angle to shoot, Mihei hit in the mouth by the falling chain itself, Mugikura watched on stage, Tarumi and Nanjo photographed embracing each other -- eliminates six of the seven, leaving Masuyama as the only suspect who could have fired the shot.
